headline: Wikipedia Shrinks to a Half-Hour Walk
lede: This location-aware project turns the encyclopedia into a neighborhood guide. It keeps your position in the browser, then surfaces nearby places, histories, and oddities without exposing where you are in shared links.

headline: Docker Is a Stack of Ordinary Processes
lede: Containers are not miniature virtual machines. They are processes assembled from namespaces, cgroups, filesystem tricks, and networking machinery—simple at the command line, intricate underneath.

headline: Models Hide Messages in Plain Sight
lede: Fable can encode text into the geometry and scenery of an SVG, then recover much of it from a screenshot. The experiment is still conspicuous and fragile, but it sketches a quiet machine-to-machine channel worth watching.

headline: The AI Boom Still Mistakes Motion for Progress
lede: Jev’s story is less a collapse than a warning about how quickly technical claims become market narratives. Speed, structured output, and a polished label do not remove the old problems of error, cost, and unreliable reasoning.
pullquote: A louder benchmark story does not make an unreliable system reliable.

headline: Dijkstra Rejects the Dream of Easy Programming
lede: In 1978, Edsger Dijkstra argued that natural language was too ambiguous to serve as a dependable programming medium. His case for notation, constraints, and explicitness now reads like an early warning about delegating specifications to fluent machines.

headline: AI Searches Beyond a Field’s Familiar Ideas
lede: The Alien Sampling paper treats novelty as a search problem: recombine reusable ideas while penalizing combinations too readily available to existing research communities. Its results suggest broader portfolios without abandoning coherence, though the corpus still defines what can be found.

headline: 29 of 35 Models Choose the Same Human Critique
lede: Asked for a controversial opinion about humanity, most text models converged on tribalism, loyalty, and status. The small experiment does not reveal independent machine beliefs; it reveals how similar training material and prompts can make different systems sound alike.

headline: Chrome Brings Live HTML Into Canvas
lede: The experimental HTML-in-Canvas API combines canvas and WebGL presentation with the DOM’s accessibility, selection, forms, and inspection tools. It is a clean answer to a persistent browser tradeoff, still bounded by origin-trial status and JavaScript-driven performance costs.

headline: OpenShell Sandboxes Fleets of Autonomous Agents
lede: OpenShell. Isolate files, syscalls, processes, networks, credentials. Add policy review, a local gateway, a CLI, and Kubernetes support. The goal: useful agents with a smaller blast radius.

headline: Heinlein Makes the Case for Ordinary Decency
lede: This 1952 essay looks past the crimes and scandals that dominate attention to the quieter work of sustaining a society. Neighbors help, teachers persist, nurses care, and institutions endure—an optimistic argument that asks whether distrust is as realistic as it feels.
